proof.criterion: Spec `Proven on` — "a run with the third-party source made unreachable for one job (a negative control)", the tester's failure 1
proof.surface: GitHub Actions in sjawhar/legion: one job of the scratch pull request sjawhar/legion#2520, opened off this branch for the two controls and closed after they were quoted
proof.command: The `Unreachable Source Control` workflow, run 40946334621 (https://github.com/sjawhar/legion/actions/runs/40946334621), at head f3024ecb
proof.observed: Every step green. The first step put registry-1.docker.io, index.docker.io, auth.docker.io, mirror.gcr.io and proxy.golang.org at 0.0.0.0. The job then pulled ghcr.io/sjawhar/legion/ci@sha256:5498ba57 (`pulled sha256:1fd1a8eb`), ran it (`the NATS copy answered on 127.0.0.1:32768`), and built Go over a cold module cache with `go build ./cmd/legion`: 92 `go: downloading` lines through `direct`, then `legion (devel)`.
proof.negativeControl: In the same run, the step before the pull asked the old registry for the same image and had to fail: `docker pull mirror.gcr.io/library/nats:2.10 failed, as it must`. A green run where the block did nothing is therefore not possible.

proof.criterion: The tester's failure 2 — the gate passed a Dockerfile that builds FROM a third-party image named through an ARG default
proof.surface: The gate .github/scripts/check-ci-images.sh and its harness, which ci.yaml's ci-images and test jobs run
proof.observed: `Results: 67 passed, 0 failed` (65 before the tester's case, 67 with it), including the tester's own `a third-party default fails` and `names the image the build fetches`; the tester's case is in the file word for word and was not edited. On the real tree the gate prints `.github/ci-images.yaml holds 12 row(s), 12 of them in the package; 35 reference(s) in 32 file(s) of CI's reach name one of those rows; of 6274 text file(s) swept, the 29 that name mirror.gcr.io are all in the exception list`, exit 0. scan_dockerfile now substitutes each ARG's default into the FROM and reads the result; a re-declaration without `=` keeps the earlier default, and a variable declared with no default anywhere is still skipped, because whoever runs the build passes it.
proof.negativeControl: The tester's case is the red one: `ARG BASE_IMAGE=docker.io/library/debian:trixie-slim` with `FROM ${BASE_IMAGE} AS build` fails the gate and names docker.io/library/debian:trixie-slim. It failed to fail before this change and fails now.

proof.criterion: The tester's failure 4 and the architect's fifth fix — a pull request that adds a row must not race its own gate
proof.surface: The copy script and the gate, driven over fixtures with a fake crane first on PATH and the gate's documented CI_IMAGES_MANIFEST_HEAD seam, so no case reaches the network
proof.observed: `Results: 20 passed, 0 failed`. The ordering case is the point: a fixture whose package lacks one row fails check 7 of the gate before .github/scripts/mirror-ci-images.sh runs, and passes it after. In ci.yaml the two are one job, ci-images, whose steps are the copy then the gate, and which is in ci-ok's needs and in ci_filter_coverage.py's ALWAYS_RUN, so its failure fails the required check. mirror-images.yaml keeps the copy for a push to main and has lost its pull_request trigger.
proof.negativeControl: Three more cases of the same harness: a row the package already holds is not copied again; a copy that lands at another digest fails naming the row and both digests; and the ordering case's `before` half, which is the gate refusing the row the package lacks.

proof.criterion: Spec version 6, from dispatch://INFRA-333 — "in a fresh worker pod, `go test ./...` in `packages/daemon` downloads no module", read as the architect settled it: no network read and no time lost, the `go: downloading` lines coming from the image's own cache
proof.surface: The image's own mechanism, run in the issue pod: a download cache filled the way worker.Dockerfile's `go` stage fills it, then a fresh module cache served by that cache through a `file://` proxy with the public proxy at a dead address
proof.command: cd packages/daemon && GOMODCACHE=<fresh> GOPROXY='file://<the filled cache>/cache/download|http://127.0.0.1:1' go build ./cmd/legion
proof.observed: exit 0, a 100 MB binary, 92 `go: downloading` lines, every one served from the file proxy with no network read possible. The filled cache is 380 MiB over 419 module zips, which is what the runtime stage copies to /home/legion/go/pkg/mod/cache/download, owned by the runtime user; the extracted trees (2.2 GiB) stay out of the image. The toolchain stage rewrites /opt/go/go.env's GOPROXY to `file:///home/legion/go/pkg/mod/cache/download|https://proxy.golang.org|direct`, which is how the cache reaches a role: a pod sets GOMODCACHE=/legion/go/mod, the issue volume, and a container's environment outranks an image ENV.
proof.negativeControl: The same fresh module cache with the file proxy taken away, GOPROXY='http://127.0.0.1:1' alone -> exit 1, `go: github.com/jackc/pgx/v5@v5.11.0: Get "http://127.0.0.1:1/...": dial tcp 127.0.0.1:1: connect: connection refused`.

proof.criterion: Spec version 6, from dispatch://INFRA-318 — a workflow runs the scripts/e2e proofs on a GitHub-hosted runner, started by a label or by workflow_dispatch with a script name and nightly on main, uploading each run's evidence
proof.surface: GitHub Actions in sjawhar/legion: the `e2e` label on this pull request, which is the one label-started workflow of this repository
proof.command: gh pr edit 2512 --add-label e2e, which started E2E proofs run 40957651922 (https://github.com/sjawhar/legion/actions/runs/40957651922) at head a744ce61
proof.observed: The label started the workflow at this head, one job per proof over the five scripts a hosted runner can run. The run was still queued when this phase completed: every workflow of this repository was queued behind GitHub's own backlog at the time (main's own docs-pages runs had been pending for over an hour), which is an Actions capacity condition and not a property of this change. The tester reads its verdict and its artifacts with `gh run view 40957651922` and `gh run download 40957651922`; this is the one line of this handoff whose result is not yet in hand, and it is named as such in the pull request body.
proof.negativeControl: The select job's refusal path, read from the workflow: a workflow_dispatch naming a script of the `elsewhere` list fails with `scripts/e2e/<name> needs <what its header says>`, and a script in neither list fails the run, so a new script under scripts/e2e/ joins one list or the workflow stops. The list file and the scripts were checked against each other in the pod: 20 scripts present, 0 unlisted, 0 stale rows.

scripts/e2e/README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/kubernetes.md, docs/solutions/github/an-image-pull-that-fails-in-ci-…-INFRA-567.md, docs/solutions/github/join-a-job-to-the-ci-router.md: the prose each change falsified
deviations: dispatch-session-settings.sh is in the e2e workflow's refused list, not among the six the architect named. Sami answered dispatch://INFRA-567/ask/4fd91c78: no API key goes into sjawhar/legion, and a smoke test that calls a model runs in the deployment repository on workload identity federation. The script's own prerequisite check refuses without a key for each of its two models, so a hosted row for it could only ever refuse. The architect accepted this.

stage4a-sandbox-runtime.sh is in no workflow. It needs the production cluster's restricted kubeconfig, an operator context, a local Docker daemon and agent-secrets, which no GitHub-hosted runner has and no repository secret supplies. Sami settled it on dispatch://INFRA-567/ask/520c4968: what the daemon may do on a cluster is the operator's, not this repository's.

The acceptance line naming parked-decision-devbox.sh is dropped by the architect: no such file exists in sjawhar/legion (`grep -rIln 'parked-decision'` over the tree finds nothing, and scripts/e2e holds 20 .sh files, none of that name).

The warm Go module cache reaches a role as a `file://` proxy rather than as its GOMODCACHE, because a pod sets GOMODCACHE=/legion/go/mod and a container's environment outranks an image ENV. The architect settled the reading: no network read and no time lost, and manifest.go is not touched, because the issue volume's cache is shared across a pod's roles and an image path would lose that.
openQuestions: E2E proofs run 40957651922 was queued, not settled, when this phase completed; GitHub's own backlog had every workflow of this repository queued, main's docs-pages runs for over an hour. Its verdict and its evidence artifacts are the tester's to read.

The docs-pages control run on the scratch pull request (40946334589, head f3024ecb) was still pending for the same reason, behind the `pages` concurrency group, where main's own runs were also pending. What it would show is the two steps only main reaches: docs-site.yaml's upload-pages-artifact step and docs-pages.yaml's deploy job skipping on a branch. The change that gives those steps a surface, workflow_dispatch on docs-pages.yaml with deploy held to main, is in the branch and is readable; the run is not.

No CI job prints `go env GOPROXY`, so that the workflow-level value reaches a CI job's go command is read from GitHub's documented env semantics and a green Go lane. The behaviour itself is proven directly, twice, against the same go1.27.1.
discoveredComplexity: A workflow_dispatch cannot start a workflow whose file is not yet on the default branch, so the two controls had to run through a pull_request event: the scratch pull request for the unreachable-source job and for docs-pages, and the `e2e` label for the e2e workflow.

Adding GOPROXY to a workflow's env would have made every claimed go command of ci.yaml fall to `reads everything` in check-ci-filters.sh, which refuses an env name outside ENV_ALLOWED; GOPROXY is now in that list with its reason.
